title: Marketplace publish: hello-world flow + contract cheatsheet
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational "hello-world" playbook for publishing a partner tile to a cloud marketplace with minimal friction. It pairs a minimal copy set (tile + short description + 2 usage snippets) with an aligned contract/billing checklist so legal, finance, and product can sign off quickly.

Intended audience:
- Partner PM / Integration PM (primary)
- GTM ops / Partnerships
- Legal (quick scan)
- Engineering (QA + onboarding)

Success criteria (what "good" looks like):
- Tile accepted by marketplace scan on first submission
- Billing SKU maps to internal metering and partner contract (no manual reconciliation)
- <72h partner onboarding time from access request to trial enabled
- Basic telemetry (installs, trial starts) appear in console within 24h of launch

Quick TL;DR flow (1-page):
1) Intake: partner completes short intake form (tile, logo, short description, contact, desired billing model).
2) Preflight: GTM ops runs checklist below (legal flags, data residency, KMS).
3) Copy freeze: finalize hero tile copy + 1-paragraph long description + 2 usage examples.
4) Asset prep: screenshots, logos, thumbnails, icon (512x512 png), marketing URL, support email.
5) Contract: confirm billing model + trial terms + data residency clause. Use contract cheatsheet mapping.
6) Submission: engineering attaches package + telemetry hooks; submit to marketplace.
7) Post-approval: enable trial SKUs, update docs, send partner onboarding email.

Minimal copy set (ready-to-paste variants):
- Tile title (<= 60 chars): "Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM inference"
- Short tagline (<= 120 chars): "Serve LLMs at predictable latency and cost — hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- 1-paragraph long description (300–400 chars): "Redwood Inference provides a production-grade runtime for serving large language models with predictable latency and transparent unit economics. Choose hosted API, dedicated capacity, or private deployments to meet security and SLA needs. Includes tracing, rollout controls, and cost optimization tools."
- Key bullets (3): "Production SLOs & SLAs", "Cost-aware batching & caching", "Private VPC & on-prem options"

Two usage snippets (for tile & docs):
- Getting started (2 lines): "Create an API key, pick a model from the catalog, and call /v1/generate. Sample: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{\"prompt\":\"Hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
- Integration example (2 lines): "Use Redwood SDK to pin model versions and enable canary rollout: Redwood.client.rollouts.create({model:'redwood-xl-v1', traffic:{canary:0.05}})"

Asset checklist (must-haves before submission):
- Company logo (SVG + PNG 512x512)
- Tile hero screenshot (1280x720 png) + 2 UI screenshots (desktop)
- Short support blurb (one-line) and support email (support@redwood.ai)
- Marketing URL (https://www.redwood.ai/marketplace/partner-name)
- One-liner about data residency options if requested
- Contact for commercial escalation (name, email)

Technical & telemetry requirements (engineering):
- Metering: expose usage events to billing pipeline (token counts / embedding units)
- Telemetry hook: marketplace install -> generate customer org ID in console -> report install event
- Auth: support API-key-based access for trial SKUs; supply onboarding script for partners
- SSO: if partner requires SSO/SAML, note in intake and route to Private deployment checklist

Contract & billing cheatsheet (mapping quick guide for legal/finance):
- Billing model mapping:
  - Marketplace metered usage -> map to internal per-token SKU. Ensure precision: marketplace reports "compute units" must map to token units; define conversion in CLA (e.g., 1 marketplace unit = 10k input tokens).
  - Flat monthly reservation (Dedicated) -> ensure invoice schedule matches reserved capacity charge cadence.
  - Trial vouchers -> create trial SKU that grants N free tokens; tie to marketplace trial ID.
- Data & security flags to watch for:
  - Data residency clause requested? -> route to Private deployment preflight.
  - KMS/HSM requirement? -> capture required key ops in intake, escalate to infra for feasibility.
  - Audit/logging retention beyond default? -> note and include in SOW if >90 days.
- Liability / Support SLAs (suggested template language):
  - "Redwood will provide commercially reasonable efforts to meet latency SLOs documented in the Dedicated offering. See appendix for out-of-scope events."
  - Keep indemnity caps aligned to existing partner master agreement (don't invent new terms in tile-level attachments).
- Pricing & commission notes for sales ops:
  - Prefer marketplace metered SKU with a 70/30 revenue share default (adjust per partner agreement).
  - If partner requests custom billing cadence, require finance sign-off (use GTMP-402).

Acceptance QA (for product/eng):
- Tile content validation: no truncated lines, image checksum matches size, links resolve
- Security scan: no secrets in assets, support email reachable, contact exists in CRM
- Billing / telemetry smoke test: create a sandbox purchase -> confirm token usage seen in billing logs within 30 min
- Trial flow: verify trial grant, trial consumption, and trial-to-paid conversion signal to partner dashboard

Launch comms (short templates):
- Partner email to customers: "We’re launching on [Marketplace]. Try Redwood Inference free for 14 days — enable via the marketplace tile and your trial tokens will be provisioned automatically."
- Internal standup note: "Tile for [Partner] submitted to [Marketplace] on [date]. Owners: @Ethan (ops), @Maya (eng), @Ava (GTM). Target approval: +7 business days."

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Marketplace expects a 1,500 char long description limit on some vendors — check for vendor-specific truncation and prepare a 1,400 char variant.
- Confirm exact icon asset specs for Azure marketplace (they want 300x300 and transparent bg).
- Clarify whether partner requires reseller contract vs. marketplace listing revenue share.

Launch timeline (example):
- Day 0: intake complete + copy freeze
- Day 1–3: asset prep + legal billing mapping
- Day 4–6: eng QA + telemetry hooks
- Day 7: submit to marketplace
- Day 8–15: marketplace review window (dependent on vendor)
- Post-approval Day 1: enable trial SKUs + onboarding email

Appendix (short):
- Quick copy variants for AB test:
  - Variant A title: "Fast, predictable LLM inference — Redwood"
  - Variant B title: "Run LLMs at scale with low latency"
- Short defensive copy for sensitive categories: "Redwood does not train on customer data by default. See our data handling policy at /docs/security."

If you review this, please: mark status to in_review when ready and ping #marketplace-launch with the intake link.

Notes: this doc is intentionally minimal so partners can paste copy directly into the vendor UI. Keep a copy of final assets in repo: github:repo/marketplace-assets/partner-name.
